mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reflects an accommodative monetary policy that reduces the discount rate applied to equity valuations.
failure_condition: The correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day S&P 500 returns is positive in more than 55% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) falls below 2.0%, it signals aggressive monetary easing that boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 55% of periods where FEDFUNDS < 2.0%, the 5-day forward returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a deteriorating labor market, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in less than 45% of periods where PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises.

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 6.0%), a higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as it reflects worsening economic conditions that reduce corporate profitability.
failure_condition: The correlation between UNRATE and 60-day S&P 500 returns is positive in more than 55% of 3-year rolling windows during periods when UNRATE > 6.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as it reflects strong consumer confidence and economic activity that supports corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST and 20-day S&P 500 returns is negative in more than 55% of 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1000 thousand units, it signals robust economic growth that drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In more than 55% of periods where HOUST > 1000, the 60-day forward returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days by boosting corporate revenue expectations.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in less than 45% of periods where HOUST increases and RSAFS increases.

mechanism_narrative: In a housing market downturn (HOUST < 900), a further decline in housing starts signals a deepening economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending weakens.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST and 60-day S&P 500 returns is positive in more than 55% of 3-year rolling windows during periods when HOUST < 900.
